svg.text: THE RACE — one room, overlapping stays
Room R-101 is free. Three guests reserve at once:
T1 ∩ T2 overlap on Mar 5 — only one may win
T3 is a DIFFERENT room → runs fully in parallel
naive code checks, then inserts — both pass the check
R-102 takes its own lock — zero waiting
3. res = new Reservation(seq++, room, guest, stay, cost)
SCAN + INSERT inside one lock ⇒ check-then-act is atomic ✓
reserveAny() would retry the next room
of that type instead of failing outright
Ana out on the 6th, Cy in on the 6th ⇒ 6 < 6 is FALSE
same room, back-to-back, no special case ✓
THE LIFECYCLE — State pattern, one class per state
CheckedInState rejects it — the rule lives in the state class,
not in an if-ladder inside the orchestrator
Terminal states keep the record but stop blocking —
history survives, inventory frees itself. No row is deleted.
Honest gap: nobody auto-fires markNoShow() — no scheduler here,
an operator calls it. A nightly sweep is the production answer.

g.text: WHY NOT A room.status FLAG?
A room is not "booked" — it is booked
for a WINDOW. One boolean cannot hold
an interval, so availability is derived
by scanning that room's reservations.
Cancel therefore frees the dates for free.
SCALE CEILING (be honest)
The overlap scan is O(reservations per
room) — fine for a hotel, not for a
multi-year chain. Upgrade: an interval
tree per room, or a DB EXCLUDE
constraint on (room_id, daterange).
